rounds.text: The EIH Associated Hotels Ltd (EIHAHOTELS) stock currently trades at a P/E ratio of 19.7x, which is significantly below the sector benchmark of 26.5x [E4]. This suggests that the market may be undervaluing the company's earnings potential relative to its peers. Additionally, the price-to-book (P/B) ratio stands at 2.93x, indicating a substantial discount compared to the sector median of 2.21x [E7], further supporting the notion that the stock is trading below intrinsic value. Despite these favorable metrics, the company's stock price has only risen by 18% within its recent 52-week range [E5]. This underperformance relative to its peers and historical performance suggests that investors may be overlooking the potential for significant growth. The compounded sales growth over the last five years is a robust 31%, outpacing both the sector median of 12.9% and the trailing twelve months (TTM) growth rate of -8% [E15, E17]. This strong historical growth coupled with the company's ability to accelerate earnings growth by 13% over one year [E57] indicates a solid foundation for future performance. Furthermore, the recent increase in capital work-in-progress (CWIP) from ₹47 Cr in Mar 2026 to ₹108.9 Cr in Mar 2027 represents a significant 176.5% jump [E41]. This capex build-up phase suggests ongoing growth investments, which are crucial for future revenue and profitability. In summary, the evidence points towards EIH Associated Hotels Ltd being underappreciated by the market, with its current valuation suggesting it is trading below its intrinsic value relative to both historical performance and sector benchmarks. The compounded sales growth over recent years and the upcoming capex investments indicate a promising outlook for future earnings growth.
